details:
World creators should still be able to use Udon for normal world functionality and safety systems, but I think there should be additional protections when a world is being used for a Group instance.

One example is forced teleportation.

A world may use Udon teleportation for legitimate purposes, such as respawning a player who goes out of bounds. However, world Udon should not be usable as a moderation tool to repeatedly teleport, isolate, remove, or otherwise target specific players in a Group instance.

For Group instances, moderation should be handled through the Group's authorized moderation system instead.

World Udon could still perform legitimate functions such as out-of-bounds recovery and normal world mechanics, but moderation-related actions against players should respect the authority of the Group hosting the instance.

I think this would create a clearer separation:

World Udon manages the world.

Group Moderation manages the Group instance.

For example, if Udon detects that a player has fallen outside the playable area, teleporting that player back to a valid location would still be allowed.

However, using Udon to repeatedly force a particular player into another location as a punishment or as a substitute for Group moderation should not be treated the same way.

This would let world creators continue building necessary world systems while giving Group instances better protection from world-based moderation systems being used against their members or staff.
title: Limit World Udon Moderation in Group Instances
